1.1: And Mo’aḇ revolted against Yisra’ĕl after the death of Aḥaḇ.
1.2: And Aḥazyahu fell through the lattice of his upper room in Shomeron, and was injured, and sent messengers and said to them, “Go, inquire of Ba’al-Zeḇuḇ, the mighty one of Eqron, if I shall recover from this injury.”
1.3: But a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Ĕliyah the Tishbite, “Rise up, go up to meet the messengers of the meleḵ of Shomeron, and say to them, ‘Is it because there is no Elohim in Yisra’ĕl that you are going to inquire of Ba’al-Zeḇuḇ, the mighty one of Eqron?’
1.4: “So therefore, thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘You are not going to get out of the bed to which you have gone up, for you shall certainly die.’ ” And Ĕliyahu went.
1.5: And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, “Why have you come back?”
1.6: And they said to him, “A man came up to meet us, and said to us, ‘Go, return to the meleḵ who sent you, and say to him, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Is it because there is no Elohim in Yisra’ĕl that you are sending to Ba’al-Zeḇuḇ, the mighty one of Eqron? Therefore you are not going to get out of the bed to which you have gone up, for you shall certainly die.’ ” ’ ”
1.7: And he said to them, “What was the man like who came up to meet you and spoke to you these words?”
1.8: And they answered him, “He was a hairy man, and wore a leather girdle around his waist.” And he said, “It is Ĕliyahu the Tishbite.”
1.9: He then sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men. And he went up to him, and see, he was sitting on the top of a hill. And he spoke to him, “Man of Elohim, the meleḵ has said, ‘Come down!’ ”
1.10: And Ĕliyahu answered and said to the captain of fifty, “And if I am a man of Elohim, let fire come down from the shamayim and consume you and your fifty men.” And fire came down from the shamayim and consumed him and his fifty.
1.11: He then sent another captain of fifty with his fifty men to him. And he answered and said to him, “Man of Elohim, this is what the meleḵ said, ‘Come down at once!’ ”
1.12: And Ĕliyahu answered and said to them, “If I am a man of Elohim, let fire come down from the shamayim and consume you and your fifty men.” And a fire of Elohim came down from the shamayim and consumed him and his fifty.
1.13: And again he sent a third captain of fifty with his fifty men. And the third captain of fifty went up, and came and fell on his knees before Ĕliyahu, and pleaded with him, and said to him, “Man of Elohim, please let my life and the life of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes.
1.14: “See, fire has come down from the shamayim and burned up the first two captains of fifties with their fifties. But let my life be precious in your eyes.”
1.15: And the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Ĕliyahu, “Go down with him; do not be afraid of him.” So he rose up and went down with him to the meleḵ,
1.16: and spoke to him, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Ba’al-Zeḇuḇ, the mighty one of Eqron, is it because there is no Elohim in Yisra’ĕl to inquire of His word? Therefore you are not going to get out of the bed to which you have gone up, for you shall certainly die.’ ”
1.17: And he died, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which Ĕliyahu had spoken. And Yahoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Yahoram son of Yahoshaphat meleḵ of Yahuḏah, for he had no son.
1.18: And the rest of the acts of Aḥazyahu which he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl?

10.1: And Aḥaḇ had seventy sons in Shomeron. And Yahu wrote letters and sent to Shomeron, to the rulers of Yizre’ĕl, to the elders, and to the guardians of Aḥaḇ, saying,
10.2: “And now, when this letter comes to you, since your master’s sons are with you, and you have chariots and horses, and a walled city, and weapons,
10.3: choose the best and most upright of your master’s sons, and appoint him on his father’s throne, and fight for your master’s house.”
10.4: And they were greatly afraid, and said, “Look, two melaḵim have not stood before him, how do we stand, we?”
10.5: And he who was over the house, and he who was over the city, the elders also, and the guardians, sent to Yahu, saying, “We are your servants, and all that you say to us we do. We do not appoint anyone to reign. Do what is good in your eyes.”
10.6: And he wrote a second letter to them, saying, “If you are for me, and if you obey my voice, take the heads of the men, your master’s sons, and come to me at Yizre’ĕl by this time tomorrow.” Now the meleḵ’s sons, seventy beings, were with the great men of the city, who brought them up.
10.7: And it came to be, when the letter came to them, that they took the meleḵ’s sons and slew them, seventy men, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Yizre’ĕl.
10.8: Then a messenger came and informed him, saying, “They have brought the heads of the meleḵ’s sons.” And he said, “Make them two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning.”
10.9: And it came to be, in the morning, that he went out and stood, and said to all the people, “You are righteous. Look, I conspired against my master and slew him, but who smote all these?
10.10: “Know now that not one word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke concerning the house of Aḥaḇ falls to the ground, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has done what He spoke by His servant Ĕliyahu.”
10.11: And Yahu smote all those left of the house of Aḥaḇ in Yizre’ĕl, and all his great men and his friends and his priests, until he left him without a survivor.
10.12: And he rose up to go, and went to Shomeron. On the way, at Bĕyth Ĕqeḏ of the Shepherds,
10.13: Yahu met the brothers of Aḥazyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and said, “Who are you?” And they answered, “We are brothers of Aḥazyahu, and we have come down to greet the sons of the meleḵ and the sons of the queen mother.”
10.14: And he said, “Take them alive!” So they took them alive, and slew them at the well of Bĕyth Ĕqeḏ, forty-two men, and he left none of them.
10.15: And he left there and met Yahonaḏaḇ son of Rĕḵaḇ, coming to meet him, and baraḵ him and said to him, “Is your heart right, as my heart is toward your heart?” And Yahonaḏaḇ answered, “It is.” “If it is, give me your hand.” And he gave him his hand, and he took him up to him into the chariot.
10.16: And he said, “Come with me, and see my ardor for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” And they made him ride in his chariot.
10.17: And he came to Shomeron, and smote all those left of Aḥaḇ in Shomeron, till he had destroyed them, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He spoke to Ĕliyahu.
10.18: And Yahu gathered all the people and said to them, “Aḥaḇ served Ba’al a little; Yahu serves him much.
10.19: “And now, call to me all the prophets of Ba’al, all his servants, and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I have a great slaughtering to make to Ba’al. Anyone who is lacking shall not live!” But Yahu did this deceptively, in order to destroy the servants of Ba’al.
10.20: And Yahu said, “Proclaim an assembly for Ba’al.” So they proclaimed it.
10.21: And Yahu sent throughout all Yisra’ĕl, and all the servants of Ba’al came, so that there was not a man left who did not come. And they came into the house of Ba’al, and the house of Ba’al was filled from end to end.
10.22: And he said to him who was over the wardrobe, “Bring out garments for all the servants of Ba’al.” And he brought out garments for them.
10.23: And Yahu and Yahonaḏaḇ son of Rĕḵaḇ went into the house of Ba’al, and said to the servants of Ba’al, “Search and see that no servants of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are here with you, but only the servants of Ba’al.”
10.24: So they went in to make offerings and burnt offerings. Now Yahu had appointed for himself eighty men on the outside, and had said, “The man who lets escape of the men whom I have brought into your hands - his life for his life!”
10.25: And it came to be, when he had finished making the burnt offering, Yahu said to the guard and to the officers, “Go in, smite them, let no one come out!” And they smote them with the edge of the sword, and the guards and the officers threw them out, and went into the inner room of the house of Ba’al,
10.26: and brought out the pillars of the house of Ba’al and burned them,
10.27: and broke down the statue of Ba’al, and broke down the house of Ba’al and made it a latrine to this day.
10.28: Thus Yahu destroyed Ba’al out of Yisra’ĕl.
10.29: However, Yahu did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin, from the golden calves that were at Bĕyth Ĕl and Dan.
10.30: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Yahu, “Because you have done well by doing what is right in My eyes, and have done to the house of Aḥaḇ all that was in My heart, your sons are going to sit on the throne of Yisra’ĕl to the fourth generation.”
10.31: But Yahu did not guard to walk in the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl with all his heart. For he did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ’am, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin.
10.32: In those days 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 began to cut off some in Yisra’ĕl. And Ḥaza’ĕl smote them throughout all the border of Yisra’ĕl,
10.33: from the Yardĕn to the sun-rising: all the land of Gil’aḏ - the Gaḏites, and the Re’uḇĕnites, and the Menashshites - from Aro’ĕr, which is by the wadi Arnon, including Gil’aḏ and Bashan.
10.34: And the rest of the acts of Yahu, and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl?
10.35: So Yahu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Shomeron. And Yaho’aḥaz his son reigned in his place.
10.36: And the days that Yahu reigned over Yisra’ĕl in Shomeron were twenty-eight years.

11.1: And Athalyahu was the mother of Aḥazyahu. And when she saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the offspring of the reign.
11.2: But Yahosheḇa, the daughter of Meleḵ Yoram, sister of Aḥazyahu, took Yo’ash son of Aḥazyahu, and stole him away from among the sons of the meleḵ’s sons who were put to death. So they hid him and his nurse in the bedroom, from Athalyahu, and he was not put to death.
11.3: And he remained with her in hiding in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for six years, while Athalyahu was reigning over the land.
11.4: And in the seventh year Yahoyaḏa sent and brought the commanders of hundreds, with the Karites and the runners, and brought them into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to him. And he made a covenant with them and took an oath from them in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and showed them the son of the meleḵ.
11.5: And he commanded them, saying, “This is what you are to do: One-third of you who come in on the Shabbath are to be on guard in the meleḵ’s house,
11.6: and one-third at the gate of Sur, and one-third at the gate behind the runners. And you shall be on guard in the house, lest it be broken down.
11.7: “And the two detachments of you who are going out on the Shabbath shall be on guard in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for the meleḵ.
11.8: “And you shall surround the meleḵ on all sides, every man with his weapons in his hand. And whoever comes within the ranks, let him be put to death. And be with the meleḵ as he goes out and as he comes in.”
11.9: So the commanders of the hundreds did according to all that Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn commanded. And each of them took his men who were going in on the Shabbath, with those who were going out on the Shabbath, and came to Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn.
11.10: And the kohĕn gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and shields which had belonged to Meleḵ Dawiḏ, that were in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
11.11: And the runners stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, all around the meleḵ, from the right side of the House to the left side of the House, by the altar and the House.
11.12: And he brought out the son of the meleḵ and put on him the diadem and the Witness. And they appointed him to reign and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, “Let the meleḵ live!”
11.13: And Athalyahu heard the noise of the runners, the people, and she came to the people, into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
11.14: and looked and saw the meleḵ standing by a column, according to the ruling, and the chiefs and the trumpeters were beside the meleḵ, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. And Athalyahu tore her garments and cried out, “Treason! Treason!”
11.15: And Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn commanded the commanders of the hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, “Take her outside the ranks, and slay with the sword whoever follows her.” For the kohĕn had said, “Do not let her be killed in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
11.16: So they took hold of her, and she went by way of the horses’ entrance to the meleḵ’s house, and was put to death there.
11.17: And Yahoyaḏa made a covenant between 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the meleḵ and the people, to be the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - also between the meleḵ and the people.
11.18: And all the people of the land went to the house of Ba’al, and broke it down. They completely broke up its altars and images, and slew Mattan the priest of Ba’al before the altars. And the kohĕn appointed inspectors over the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
11.19: and took the commanders of hundreds, and the Karites, and the runners, and all the people of the land. And they brought the meleḵ down from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and went by way of the gate of the runners to the meleḵ’s house. And he sat on the throne of the melaḵim.
11.20: And all the people of the land rejoiced. And the city had rest, for they had slain Athalyahu with the sword in the meleḵ’s house.
11.21: Yaho’ash was seven years old when he began to reign.

12.1: Yaho’ash began to reign in the seventh year of Yahu, and he reigned forty years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Tsiḇyah of Be’ĕrsheḇa.
12.2: And Yaho’ash did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all the days in which Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn instructed him.
12.3: However, the high places were not taken away; the people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places.
12.4: And Yaho’ash said to the kohenim, “All the silver of the qodesh gifts that are brought into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the silver coming over, each man’s assessment silver, all the silver that a man purposes in his heart to bring into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
12.5: let the kohenim take for themselves, each from his friend. And let them repair the damages of the House, wherever there is damage.”
12.6: And it came to be, by the twenty-third year of Meleḵ Yaho’ash, that the kohenim had not repaired the damages of the House,
12.7: and Meleḵ Yaho’ash called Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn and the other kohenim, and said to them, “Why have you not repaired the damages of the House? And now, do not take any more silver from your friends, but give it for repairing the damages of the House.”
12.8: And the kohenim agreed that they would neither receive any more silver from the people, nor repair the damages of the House.
12.9: And Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn took a chest, and bored a hole in its lid, and put it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And the kohenim who guarded the door put there all the silver that was brought into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
12.10: And it came to be, whenever they saw that there was much silver in the chest, that the meleḵ’s scribe and the kohĕn ha’gadol came up and put it in bags, and counted the silver that was found in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
12.11: and gave the silver, weighed out, into the hands of those who did the work, who had the oversight of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
12.12: and to stonemasons and stone-cutters, and for buying timber and hewn stone to repair the damage of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and for all that was paid out to repair the House.
12.13: However there were not made for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 basins of silver, snuffers, sprinkling-bowls, trumpets, any objects of gold, or objects of silver, from the silver that was brought into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
12.14: for they gave that to the workmen, and they repaired the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with it.
12.15: And they did not reckon with the men into whose hand they gave the silver to be paid to workmen, for they acted trustworthily.
12.16: The silver from the trespass offerings and the silver from the sin offerings were not brought into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. It belonged to the kohenim.
12.17: And Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram went up and fought against Gath, and captured it. And Ḥaza’ĕl turned his face to go up to Yerushalayim.
12.18: And Yaho’ash meleḵ of Yahuḏah took all the qodesh gifts that his fathers, Yahoshaphat and Yahoram and Aḥazyahu, melaḵim of Yahuḏah, had qadosh, and his own qodesh gifts, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and in the meleḵ’s house, and sent them to Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram. Then he went away from Yerushalayim.
12.19: And the rest of the acts of Yo’ash, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
12.20: And his servants rose up and made a conspiracy, and smote Yo’ash in the house of Millo, which goes down to Silla.
12.21: For Yozaḵar son of Shim’ath and Yahozaḇaḏ son of Shomĕr, his servants, smote him. So he died, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of Dawiḏ. And Amatsyah his son reigned in his place.

13.1: In the twenty-third year of Yo’ash son of Aḥazyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, Yaho’aḥaz son of Yahu began to reign over Yisra’ĕl in Shomeron, and reigned seventeen years.
13.2: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and followed the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin. He did not turn away from them.
13.3: And the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against Yisra’ĕl, and He gave them into the hand of Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram, and into the hand of Ben-Haḏaḏ son of Ḥaza’ĕl, all the days.
13.4: Then Yaho’aḥaz sought the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 listened to him, for He saw the oppression of Yisra’ĕl, because the meleḵ of Aram oppressed them.
13.5: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave Yisra’ĕl a savior, so that they came out from under the hand of Aram. And the children of Yisra’ĕl dwelt in their tents as before.
13.6: However, they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Yaroḇ’am, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin, but walked in them. Moreover, the Ashĕrah also remained in Shomeron.
13.7: For He left of the army of Yaho’aḥaz only fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen, for the meleḵ of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.
13.8: And the rest of the acts of Yaho’aḥaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl?
13.9: So Yaho’aḥaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Shomeron. And Yo’ash his son reigned in his place.
13.10: In the thirty-seventh year of Yo’ash meleḵ of Yahuḏah, Yaho’ash son of Yaho’aḥaz began to reign over Yisra’ĕl in Shomeron, sixteen years.
13.11: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He did not turn away from all the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin - he walked in it.
13.12: And the rest of the acts of Yo’ash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amatsyah meleḵ of Yahuḏah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl?
13.13: So Yo’ash slept with his fathers. And Yaroḇ’am sat on his throne. And Yo’ash was buried in Shomeron with the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl.
13.14: And Elisha had become sick with the sickness in which he died. And Yo’ash the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl came down to him, and wept over his face, and said, “O my father, my father, the chariots of Yisra’ĕl and their horsemen!”
13.15: And Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and some arrows.” And he took a bow and some arrows.
13.16: And he said to the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, “Place your hand on the bow.” So he placed his hand, and Elisha placed his hands on the hands of the meleḵ,
13.17: and said, “Open the east window.” And he opened it and Elisha said, “Shoot.” And he shot. Then he said, “The arrow of deliverance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the arrow of deliverance from Aram, for you shall smite Aram at Aphĕq until it is finished.”
13.18: Then he said, “Take the arrows,” and he took them. And he said to the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, “Strike the ground,” and he struck three times, and stopped.
13.19: And the man of Elohim was wroth with him and said, “You should have smitten five or six times, then you would have smitten Aram till its utter destruction. But now you shall smite Aram only three times.”
13.20: And Elisha died, and they buried him. And the raiding bands from Mo’aḇ came into the land in the spring of the year.
13.21: And it came to be, they were burying a man, and there they saw a raiding band, and cast the man in the tomb of Elisha. And the man fell and touched the bones of Elisha, and came to life and stood on his feet.
13.22: And Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram oppressed Yisra’ĕl all the days of Yaho’aḥaz.
13.23: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 showed favor to them, and had compassion on them, and turned toward them, for the sake of His Covenant with Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Ya’aqoḇ, and would not destroy them or cast them from His presence as yet.
13.24: And Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram died. And Ben-Haḏaḏ his son reigned in his place.
13.25: And Yaho’ash son of Yaho’aḥaz recovered from the hand of Ben-Haḏaḏ, son of Ḥaza’ĕl, the cities which he had taken out of the hand of Yaho’aḥaz his father in battle. Yo’ash smote him three times, and he recovered the cities of Yisra’ĕl.

14.1: In the second year of Yo’ash son of Yo’aḥaz, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, began to reign.
14.2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yaho’addin of Yerushalayim.
14.3: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but not like his father Dawiḏ. He did according to all his father Yo’ash did.
14.4: However, the high places were not taken away. The people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places.
14.5: And it came to be, as soon as the reign was strong in his hand, that he smote his servants who had smitten his father the meleḵ.
14.6: But he did not put to death the children of the murderers, according to what is written in the Book of the Torah of Mosheh, in which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded, saying, “Fathers are not put to death for the children, and children are not put to death for the fathers, but each one is put to death for his own sin.”
14.7: He smote Eḏom in the Valley of Salt, ten thousand, and took Sela in battle, and called its name Yoqthe’ĕl to this day.
14.8: Amatsyah then sent messengers to Yaho’ash son of Yaho’aḥaz, son of Yahu, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “Come, let us look each other in the face!”
14.9: And Yaho’ash meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl sent to Amatsyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, saying, “The thistle that was in Leḇanon sent to the cedar that was in Leḇanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife.’ And a wild beast that was in Leḇanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
14.10: “You have certainly smitten Eḏom, and your heart has lifted you up. Be esteemed and stay in your house. But why do you stir up yourself to evil, that you should fall - you and Yahuḏah with you?”
14.11: But Amatsyahu did not listen, so Yaho’ash meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl went up, and he and Amatsyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah faced one another at Bĕyth Shemesh, which belongs to Yahuḏah.
14.12: And Yahuḏah was smitten before Yisra’ĕl, and they each fled to his tent.
14.13: And Yaho’ash meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl caught Amatsyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, son of Yaho’ash, son of Aḥazyahu, at Bĕyth Shemesh. And they came to Yerushalayim and he broke through the wall of Yerushalayim from the Gate of Ephrayim to the Corner Gate, four hundred ammah,
14.14: and took all the gold and silver, and all the objects that were found in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and in the treasuries of the meleḵ’s house, and hostages, and returned to Shomeron.
14.15: And the rest of the acts of Yaho’ash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amatsyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl?
14.16: So Yaho’ash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Shomeron with the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl. And Yaroḇ’am his son reigned in his place.
14.17: And Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, lived fifteen years after the death of Yaho’ash son of Yaho’aḥaz, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.
14.18: And the rest of the acts of Amatsyahu, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
14.19: And they made a conspiracy against him in Yerushalayim, and he fled to Laḵish. And they sent after him to Laḵish and killed him there,
14.20: and brought him on horses, and he was buried at Yerushalayim with his fathers in the City of Dawiḏ.
14.21: And all the people of Yahuḏah took Azaryahu, who was sixteen years old, and appointed him to reign instead of his father Amatsyahu.
14.22: He built Ĕylath and restored it to Yahuḏah, after the meleḵ slept with his fathers.
14.23: In the fifteenth year of Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, Yaroḇ’am son of Yo’ash, the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, began to reign in Shomeron, and reigned forty-one years.
14.24: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He did not turn away from all the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin.
14.25: He restored the border of Yisra’ĕl from the entrance of Ḥamath to the Sea of the Araḇah, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, which He had spoken through His servant Yonah son of Amittai, the naḇi who was from Gath Ḥĕpher.
14.26: For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saw that the affliction of Yisra’ĕl was very bitter. And there was no one, neither shut up nor left at large, to help Yisra’ĕl.
14.27: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had not said that He would blot out the name of Yisra’ĕl from under the shamayim, but saved them by the hand of Yaroḇ’am son of Yo’ash.
14.28: And the rest of the acts of Yaroḇ’am, and all that he did, and his might, how he fought, and how he recovered Dammeseq and Ḥamath for Yahuḏah in Yisra’ĕl, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl?
14.29: So Yaroḇ’am slept with his fathers, the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl. And Zeḵaryah his son reigned in his place.

15.1: In the twenty-seventh year of Yaroḇ’am meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, Azaryahu son of Amatsyah, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, began to reign.
15.2: He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeḵolyahu of Yerushalayim.
15.3: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that his father Amatsyahu did,
15.4: however, the high places were not taken away. The people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places.
15.5: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smote the meleḵ, so that he was a leper until the day of his death, and he dwelt in a separate house. And Yotham son of the meleḵ was over the house, ruling the people of the land.
15.6: And the rest of the acts of Azaryahu, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
15.7: So Azaryahu slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of Dawiḏ. And Yotham his son reigned in his place.
15.8: In the thirty-eighth year of Azaryahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, Zeḵaryahu son of Yaroḇ’am began to reign over Yisra’ĕl in Shomeron, for six months.
15.9: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as his fathers had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin.
15.10: And Shallum son of Yaḇĕsh conspired against him, and smote him in front of the people, and killed him, and reigned in his place.
15.11: And the rest of the acts of Zeḵaryah, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl.
15.12: This was the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He spoke to Yahu, saying, “Your sons to the fourth generation are going to sit on the throne of Yisra’ĕl.” And it came to be so.
15.13: Shallum son of Yaḇĕsh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziyah, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah. And he reigned a month of days in Shomeron.
15.14: And Menaḥĕm son of Gaḏi went up from Tirtsah, and came to Shomeron, and smote Shallum son of Yaḇĕsh in Shomeron and killed him, and reigned in his place.
15.15: And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy which he led, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl.
15.16: And Menaḥĕm smote Tiphsaḥ, and all who were there, and its borders, from Tirtsah. Because they did not open it to him, therefore he smote it. And he ripped open all the pregnant women.
15.17: In the thirty-ninth year of Azaryahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, Menaḥĕm son of Gaḏi began to reign over Yisra’ĕl, ten years in Shomeron.
15.18: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin, all his days.
15.19: Pul the meleḵ of Ashshur came against the land. And Menaḥĕm gave Pul a thousand kiḵars of silver, for his hand to be with him to strengthen the reign in his hand.
15.20: And Menaḥĕm exacted the silver of Yisra’ĕl, of all the mighty men of wealth, of each man fifty sheqels of silver, to give to the meleḵ of Ashshur. And the meleḵ of Ashshur turned back, and did not stay there in the land.
15.21: And the rest of the acts of Menaḥĕm, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl?
15.22: So Menaḥĕm slept with his fathers. And Peqaḥyah his son reigned in his place.
15.23: In the fiftieth year of Azaryahu the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, Peqaḥyah the son of Menaḥĕm began to reign over Yisra’ĕl in Shomeron, for two years.
15.24: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin.
15.25: And Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, a chief officer of his, conspired against him and smote him in Shomeron, in the high place of the meleḵ’s house, along with Argoḇ and Aryĕh, and with him were fifty men of Gil’aḏ. So he killed him and reigned in his place.
15.26: And the rest of the acts of Peqaḥyah, and all that he did, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl.
15.27: In the fifty-second year of Azaryahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu began to reign over Yisra’ĕl in Shomeron, for twenty years.
15.28: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He did not turn away from the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin.
15.29: In the days of Peqaḥ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, Tiḡlath-Pileser meleḵ of Ashshur came and took Iyon, and Aḇĕl Bĕyth Ma’aḵah, and Yanowaḥ, and Qeḏesh, and Ḥatsor, and Gil’aḏ, and Galil, all the land of Naphtali, and took them into exile to Ashshur.
15.30: And Hoshĕa son of Ĕlah led a conspiracy against Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, and smote him, and killed him, and reigned in his place in the twentieth year of Yotham son of Uzziyah.
15.31: And the rest of the acts of Peqaḥ, and all that he did, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl.
15.32: In the second year of Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, Yotham son of Uzziyahu, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, began to reign.
15.33: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yerusha the daughter of Tsaḏoq.
15.34: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He did according to all that his father Uzziyahu did.
15.35: However, the high places were not taken away. The people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places. He built the Upper Gate of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.36: And the rest of the acts of Yotham, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
15.37: In those days 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 began to send Retsin meleḵ of Aram and Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu against Yahuḏah.
15.38: So Yotham slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Dawiḏ his father. And Aḥaz his son reigned in his place.

16.1: In the seventeenth year of Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, Aḥaz son of Yotham, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, began to reign.
16.2: Aḥaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Yerushalayim. And he did not do what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim, as his father Dawiḏ had done.
16.3: But he walked in the way of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl, and he also made his son pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the gentiles whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had dispossessed from before the children of Yisra’ĕl.
16.4: And he slaughtered and burned incense on the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.
16.5: Then Retsin meleḵ of Aram and Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, came up to Yerushalayim, to battle. And they besieged Aḥaz but were unable to overcome him.
16.6: At that time Retsin meleḵ of Aram recovered Ĕylath for Aram, and drove the men of Yahuḏah from Ĕylath. And the Eḏomites went to Ĕylath, and have dwelt there to this day.
16.7: And Aḥaz sent messengers to Tiḡlath-Pileser meleḵ of Ashshur, saying, “I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the meleḵ of Aram and from the hand of the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, who are rising up against me.”
16.8: And Aḥaz took the silver and gold that was found in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and in the treasuries of the house of the meleḵ, and sent it as a present to the meleḵ of Ashshur.
16.9: And the meleḵ of Ashshur listened to him. And the meleḵ of Ashshur went up against Dammeseq and captured it, and exiled it to Qir, and he killed Retsin.
16.10: And Meleḵ Aḥaz went to meet Tiḡlath-Pileser meleḵ of Ashshur at Dammeseq, and saw an altar that was at Dammeseq. And Meleḵ Aḥaz sent to Uriyah the kohĕn a sketch of the altar and its pattern, according to all its workmanship.
16.11: And Uriyah the kohĕn built an altar according to all that Meleḵ Aḥaz had sent from Dammeseq. And Uriyah the kohĕn made it before Meleḵ Aḥaz came from Dammeseq.
16.12: And when the meleḵ came from Dammeseq, the meleḵ saw the altar, and the meleḵ approached the altar and made offerings on it.
16.13: And he burned his burnt offering and his grain offering. And he poured his drink offering and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
16.14: And the bronze altar which was before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 he brought from the front of the House, from between the new altar and the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and put it on the north side of the altar.
16.15: And Meleḵ Aḥaz commanded Uriyah the kohĕn, saying, “On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering, and the evening grain offering, and the meleḵ’s burnt offering, and his grain offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their grain offering, and their drink offerings. And sprinkle on it all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the slaughtering. And the bronze altar is for me to inquire by.”
16.16: And Uriyah the kohĕn did according to all that Meleḵ Aḥaz commanded.
16.17: And Meleḵ Aḥaz cut off the side panels of the stands, and removed the basins from them. And he took down the sea from the bronze oxen that were under it, and put it on a pavement of stones.
16.18: And the covered way which they had built in the House for the Shabbath, and the meleḵ’s outer entrance, he took from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, because of the meleḵ of Ashshur.
16.19: And the rest of the acts of Aḥaz which he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
16.20: So Aḥaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Dawiḏ. And Ḥizqiyahu his son reigned in his place.

17.1: In the twelfth year of Aḥaz meleḵ of Yahuḏah, Hoshĕa son of Ĕlah began to reign over Yisra’ĕl in Shomeron, for nine years.
17.2: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but not as the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl who were before him.
17.3: Shalmaneser meleḵ of Ashshur came up against him. And Hoshĕa became his servant, and rendered him a present.
17.4: But the meleḵ of Ashshur found a conspiracy in Hoshĕa, for he had sent messengers to So, meleḵ of Mitsrayim, and had not brought a present to the meleḵ of Ashshur, as year by year. And the meleḵ of Ashshur shut him up, and bound him in prison.
17.5: And the meleḵ of Ashshur went through all the land, and went up to Shomeron and besieged it for three years.
17.6: In the ninth year of Hoshĕa, the meleḵ of Ashshur captured Shomeron and exiled Yisra’ĕl to Ashshur, and settled them in Ḥalaḥ and Ḥaḇor, the River of Gozan, and in the cities of the Maḏites.
17.7: Now this came to be because the children of Yisra’ĕl had sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim - who had brought them up out of the land of Mitsrayim, from under the hand of Pharaoh meleḵ of Mitsrayim - and revered other mighty ones,
17.8: and walked in the laws of the gentiles whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had dispossessed from before the children of Yisra’ĕl, and of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl that they had made.
17.9: And the children of Yisra’ĕl secretly did matters against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim that were not right, and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower unto the walled city,
17.10: and put up for themselves pillars and Ashĕrim on every high hill and under every green tree,
17.11: and burned incense there on all the high places, like the gentiles whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had removed from their presence. And they did evil matters to provoke 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
17.12: and served the idols, of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said to them, “Do not do this.”
17.13: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 warned Yisra’ĕl and Yahuḏah, through all of His neḇi’im, and every seer, saying, “Turn back from your evil ways, and guard My Commands and My Laws, according to all the Torah which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by My servants the neḇi’im.”
17.14: But they did not listen and hardened their necks, like the necks of their fathers, who did not put their trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim,
17.15: and rejected His Laws and His Covenant that He had made with their fathers, and His Witnesses which He had witnessed against them, and went after worthlessness, and became worthless, and after the gentiles who were all around them, of whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded them not to do like them.
17.16: And they left all the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, and made for themselves a molded image, two calves, and made an Ashĕrah and bowed themselves to all the host of the shamayim, and served Ba’al,
17.17: and caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, and practiced divination and sorcery, and sold themselves to do evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to provoke Him.
17.18: So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was very enraged with Yisra’ĕl, and removed them from His presence - none was left but the tribe of Yahuḏah alone.
17.19: Yahuḏah, also, did not guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, but walked in the laws of Yisra’ĕl which they made.
17.20: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rejected all the seed of Yisra’ĕl, and afflicted them, and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until He had cast them out from His presence.
17.21: For He tore Yisra’ĕl from the house of Dawiḏ, and they made Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat meleḵ. And Yaroḇ’am drove Yisra’ĕl from following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and made them commit a great sin.
17.22: And the children of Yisra’ĕl walked in all the sins of Yaroḇ’am which he did. They did not turn away from them,
17.23: until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 removed Yisra’ĕl from His presence, as He spoke by all His servants the neḇi’im. So Yisra’ĕl was exiled from their land to Ashshur, as it is to this day.
17.24: And the meleḵ of Ashshur brought people from Baḇel, and from Kuthah, and from Awwa, and from Ḥamath, and Sepharwayim, and placed them in the cities of Shomeron instead of the children of Yisra’ĕl. And they took possession of Shomeron and dwelt in its cities.
17.25: And it came to be, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent lions among them, which kept on slaying among them.
17.26: And they spoke to the meleḵ of Ashshur, saying, “The nations whom you have removed and placed in the cities of Shomeron do not know the Right-Ruling of the Elohim of the land. And He has sent lions among them, and see, they are slaying among them because they do not know the Right-Ruling of the Elohim of the land.”
17.27: And the meleḵ of Ashshur commanded, saying, “Send one of the kohenim whom you exiled from there, to go there. Let him go and dwell there, and let him teach them the Right-Ruling of the Elohim of the land.”
17.28: And one of the kohenim whom they had exiled from Shomeron came and dwelt in Bĕyth Ĕl, and taught them how to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.29: But every nation was making mighty ones of its own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Shomeronites had made, every nation in the cities where they dwelt.
17.30: And the men of Baḇel made Sukkoth Benoth, and the men of Kuth made Nĕrḡal, and the men of Ḥamath made Ashima,
17.31: and the Awwites made Niḇḥaz and Tartaq. And the Sepharwites burned their children in fire to Aḏrammeleḵ and Anammeleḵ, the mighty ones of Sepharim.
17.32: They also revered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and from every class they made for themselves priests of the high places, who offered for them in the house of the high places.
17.33: They were revering 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and they were serving their own mighty ones, according to the ruling of the nations from among whom they had been exiled.
17.34: To this day they are doing according to the former rulings: they are not revering 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, nor do they follow their Laws or their Right-Rulings, or the Torah and Command which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded the children of Ya’aqoḇ, whose name He made Yisra’ĕl,
17.35: with whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had made a Covenant and commanded them, saying, “Do not revere other mighty ones, nor bow down to them nor serve them nor slaughter to them;
17.36: but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who brought you up from the land of Mitsrayim with great power and with an outstretched arm, Him you shall revere, and to Him you shall bow yourselves, and to Him you shall slaughter.
17.37: “And guard to do forever the Laws, and the Right-Rulings, and the Torah, and the Command which He wrote for you. And do not revere other mighty ones.
17.38: “And do not forget the Covenant that I have made with you, and do not revere other mighty ones.
17.39: “And revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, so that He delivers you from the hand of all your enemies.”
17.40: But they did not obey, and did according to their former ruling.
17.41: So these nations were revering 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and served their carved images, both their children and their children’s children. As their fathers did, they are doing to this day.

18.1: And it came to be in the third year of Hoshĕa son of Ĕlah, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, that Ḥizqiyahu son of Aḥaz, meleḵ of Yahuḏah, began to reign.
18.2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Aḇi, daughter of Zeḵaryah.
18.3: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that his father Dawiḏ did.
18.4: He took away the high places and broke the pillars, and cut down the Ashĕrah, and broke in pieces the bronze serpent which Mosheh had made, for until those days the children of Yisra’ĕl burned incense to it, and called it Neḥushtan.
18.5: He put his trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, and after him was none like him among all the melaḵim of Yahuḏah, nor who were before him,
18.6: and he clung to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. He did not turn away from following Him, but guarded His Commands, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded Mosheh.
18.7: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was with him - wherever he went he acted wisely. And he rebelled against the meleḵ of Ashshur and did not serve him.
18.8: He smote the Pelishtites, as far as Azzah and its borders - from watchtower to walled city.
18.9: And it came to be in the fourth year of Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu, which was the seventh year of Hoshĕa son of Ĕlah, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, that Shalmaneser meleḵ of Ashshur came up against Shomeron and besieged it,
18.10: and they captured it at the end of three years. In the sixth year of Ḥizqiyahu, that is the ninth year of Hoshĕa meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, Shomeron was captured.
18.11: And the meleḵ of Ashshur exiled Yisra’ĕl to Ashshur, and placed them in Ḥalaḥ and Ḥaḇor, the River of Gozan, and in the cities of the Maḏites,
18.12: because they did not obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their Elohim, but transgressed His Covenant - all that Mosheh the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded. And they did not obey nor do them.
18.13: And in the fourteenth year of Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu, Sanḥĕriḇ meleḵ of Ashshur came up against all the walled cities of Yahuḏah and captured them.
18.14: And Ḥizqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah sent to the meleḵ of Ashshur at Laḵish, saying, “I have sinned, turn away from me. I shall bear whatever you impose on me.” And the meleḵ of Ashshur imposed upon Ḥizqiyahu, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, three hundred kiḵars of silver and thirty kiḵars of gold.
18.15: And Ḥizqiyahu gave him all the silver that was found in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and in the treasuries of the meleḵ’s house.
18.16: At that time Ḥizqiyahu cut off the doors of the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the doorposts which Ḥizqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah had overlaid, and gave it to the meleḵ of Ashshur.
18.17: And the meleḵ of Ashshur sent the Tartan, and the Raḇsaris, and the Raḇshaqĕh from Laḵish, with a great army against Yerushalayim, to Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu. And they went up and came to Yerushalayim. And when they had come up, they came and stood by the channel of the upper pool, which was on the highway to the Launderer’s Field.
18.18: And they called to the meleḵ. And Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, who was over the household, and Sheḇnah the scribe, and Yo’aḥ son of Asaph, the recorder, came out to them.
18.19: And the Raḇshaqĕh said to them, “Please say to Ḥizqiyahu, ‘Thus said the great meleḵ, the meleḵ of Ashshur, “What is this trust in which you have trusted?
18.20: “You have spoken of having counsel and strength for battle, but they are only words of the lips! And in whom do you trust, that you rebel against me?
18.21: “Now look! You have put your trust in the staff of this crushed reed, Mitsrayim, on which if a man leans, it shall go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh meleḵ of Mitsrayim to all who trust in him.
18.22: “But when you say to me, ‘We trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim,’ is it not He whose high places and whose altars Ḥizqiyahu has taken away, and said to Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim, ‘Bow yourselves before this altar in Yerushalayim’?” ’
18.23: “And now, I urge you, give a pledge to my master the meleḵ of Ashshur, then I give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders on them!
18.24: “And how do you turn back the face of one commander of the least of my master’s servants, and trust in Mitsrayim for chariots and horsemen?
18.25: “Have I now come up without 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 against this place to destroy it? 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to me, ‘Go up against this land, and you shall destroy it.’ ”
18.26: Then said Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, and Sheḇnah, and Yo’aḥ to the Raḇshaqĕh, “Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. And do not speak to us in the language of Yahuḏah, in the ears of the people on the wall.”
18.27: And the Raḇshaqĕh said to them, “Has my master sent me to your master and to you to speak these words, and not to the men sitting on the wall to eat their own dung and drink their own urine, with you?”
18.28: And the Raḇshaqĕh stood and called out with a loud voice in the language of Yahuḏah, and spoke and said, “Hear the word of the great meleḵ, the meleḵ of Ashshur!
18.29: “Thus said the meleḵ, ‘Do not let Ḥizqiyahu deceive you, for he is unable to deliver you out of his hand,
18.30: and do not let Ḥizqiyahu make you trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall certainly deliver us, and this city is not given into the hand of the meleḵ of Ashshur.” ’
18.31: “Do not listen to Ḥizqiyahu, for thus said the meleḵ of Ashshur, ‘Make peace with me by a present and come out to me, and let each of you eat from his own vine and each from his own fig tree, and each of you drink the waters of his own cistern,
18.32: until I come. Then I shall take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey, and live, and not die. But do not listen to Ḥizqiyahu, when he misleads you, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall deliver us.”
18.33: ‘Has any of the mighty ones of the nations at all delivered its land from the hand of the meleḵ of Ashshur?
18.34: ‘Where are the mighty ones of Ḥamath and Arpaḏ? Where are the mighty ones of Sepharwayim and Hĕna and Iwwah? Did they deliver Shomeron from my hand?
18.35: ‘Who among all the mighty ones of the lands have delivered their land out of my hand, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 should deliver Yerushalayim from my hand?’ ”
18.36: But the people were silent and did not answer him a word, for the command of the meleḵ was, “Do not answer him.”
18.37: And Elyaqim son of Ḥilqiyahu, who was over the household, and Sheḇnah the scribe, and Yo’aḥ son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Ḥizqiyahu with their garments torn, and they reported to him the words of the Raḇshaqĕh.

19.1: And it came to be, when Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu heard it, that he tore his garments, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
19.2: and sent Elyaqim, who was over the household, and Sheḇnah the scribe, and the elders of the kohenim, covering themselves with sackcloth, to Yeshayahu the naḇi, son of Amots.
19.3: And they said to him, “Thus said Ḥizqiyahu, ‘This day is a day of distress and rebuke and scorn, for the children have come to birth but there is no power to bring forth.
19.4: ‘It could be that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim hears all the words of the Raḇshaqĕh, whom his master the meleḵ of Ashshur has sent to reproach the living Elohim, and shall rebuke the words which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim has heard. Therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.’ ”
19.5: And the servants of Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu came to Yeshayahu,
19.6: and Yeshayahu said to them, “Say this to your master, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Do not be afraid of the words which you have heard, with which the servants of the meleḵ of Ashshur have reviled Me.
19.7: “See, I am putting a spirit upon him, and he shall hear a report and return to his own land. And I shall cause him to fall by the sword in his land.” ’ ”
19.8: And the Raḇshaqĕh returned and found the meleḵ of Ashshur fighting against Liḇnah, for he had heard that he had left Laḵish.
19.9: And when the meleḵ heard concerning Tirhaqah meleḵ of Kush, “See, he has come out to fight against you,” he again sent messengers to Ḥizqiyahu, saying,
19.10: “Speak to Ḥizqiyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah, saying, ‘Do not let your Elohim in whom you trust deceive you, saying, “Yerushalayim is not given into the hand of the meleḵ of Ashshur.”
19.11: ‘See, you have heard what the melaḵim of Ashshur have done to all lands by putting them under the ban. And are you going to be delivered?
19.12: ‘Have the mighty ones of the nations delivered those whom my fathers have destroyed: Gozan and Ḥaran and Retseph, and the sons of Ĕḏen who were in Telassar?
19.13: ‘Where is the meleḵ of Ḥamath, and the meleḵ of Arpaḏ, and the meleḵ of the city of Sepharwayim, Hĕna, and Iwwah?’ ”
19.14: And Ḥizqiyahu received the letters from the hand of the messengers, and read them, and went up to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Ḥizqiyahu spread it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.15: And Ḥizqiyahu prayed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, the One who dwells between the keruḇim, You are Elohim, You alone, of all the reigns of the earth. You have made the shamayim and earth.
19.16: “Incline Your ear, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and hear. Open Your eyes, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and see. And hear the words of Sanḥĕriḇ, which he has sent to reproach the living Elohim.
19.17: “Truly, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the melaḵim of Ashshur have laid waste the nations and their lands,
19.18: and have put their mighty ones into the fire, for they were not mighty ones, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, and destroyed them.
19.19: “And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, I pray, save us from his hand, so that all the reigns of the earth know that You are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, You alone.”
19.20: Then Yeshayahu son of Amots sent to Ḥizqiyahu, saying, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘I have heard that which you have prayed to Me against Sanḥĕriḇ meleḵ of Ashshur.’
19.21: “This is the word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken concerning him, ‘The maiden, the daughter of Tsiyon, has despised you, mocked you; the daughter of Yerushalayim has shaken her head behind you!
19.22: ‘Whom have you reproached and reviled? Against whom have you raised a voice, and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Qadosh One of Yisra’ĕl!
19.23: ‘By the hand of your messengers you have reproached Aḏonai, and said, “With my many chariots I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Leḇanon. And I cut down its tall cedars, its choice cypress trees. And I enter its remotest parts, its thickest forest.
19.24: ‘I have dug and drunk strange water, and with the soles of my feet I dry up all the streams of defense.”
19.25: ‘Have you not heard long ago, I made it; from days of old I formed it? Now I have brought it to be, that you should make walled cities ruinous heaps.
19.26: ‘And their inhabitants were powerless, they were overthrown and put to shame, they were as the grass of the field and the green plants, as the grass on the house-tops and withered before it had grown.
19.27: ‘But I know your sitting down, and your going out and your coming in, and your rage against Me.
19.28: ‘Because your rage against Me and your pride have come up to My ears, I shall put My hook in your nose and My bridle in your lips, and I shall turn you back by the way which you came.
19.29: ‘And this is the sign for you: This year you eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that, and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
19.30: ‘And the remnant who have escaped of the house of Yahuḏah shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.
19.31: ‘For out of Yerushalayim comes forth a remnant, and those who escape from Mount Tsiyon - the ardor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does this.’
19.32: “Therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 concerning the meleḵ of Ashshur, ‘He does not come into this city, nor does he shoot an arrow there, nor does he come before it with shield, nor does he build a siege mound against it.
19.33: ‘By the way that he came, by the same he turns back. And he does not come into this city,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
19.34: ‘And I shall defend this city, to save it for My own sake and for the sake of Dawiḏ My servant.’ ”
19.35: And it came to be in that night that the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 went out, and smote in the camp of Ashshur one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And they rose up early in the morning and saw all of them dead bodies.
19.36: And Sanḥĕriḇ meleḵ of Ashshur broke camp and went away, and turned back, and remained in Ninewĕh.
19.37: And it came to be, as he was bowing himself in the house of Nisroḵ his mighty one, that his sons Aḏrammeleḵ and Sar’etser smote him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And his son Ĕsarḥaddon reigned in his place.

2.1: And it came to be, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was to take up Ĕliyahu to the shamayim by a whirlwind, that Ĕliyahu went with Elisha from Gilgal.
2.2: And Ĕliyahu said to Elisha, “Please remain here, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent me on to Bĕyth Ĕl.” And Elisha said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, and as your being lives, I do not leave you!” And they went down to Bĕyth Ĕl.
2.3: And the sons of the neḇi’im who were at Bĕyth Ĕl came out to Elisha, and said to him, “Do you know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is taking away your master from your head?” And he said, “I also know, be silent!”
2.4: And Ĕliyahu said to him, “Elisha, please remain here, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent me on to Yeriḥo.” And he said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, and as your being lives, I do not leave you!” And they came into Yeriḥo.
2.5: And the sons of the neḇi’im who were at Yeriḥo came to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is taking away your master from over you today?” And he said, “I also know, be silent!”
2.6: And Ĕliyahu said to him, “Please remain here, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent me on to the Yardĕn.” And he said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, and as your being lives, I do not leave you!” And the two of them went on.
2.7: And fifty men of the sons of the neḇi’im went and stood facing them at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Yardĕn.
2.8: And Ĕliyahu took his mantle, and rolled it up, and struck the water. And it was divided this way and that, so that the two of them passed over on dry ground.
2.9: And it came to be, when they had passed over, that Ĕliyahu said to Elisha, “Ask what I am to do for you, before I am taken away from you!” And Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.”
2.10: And he said, “You have made it hard to ask, yet if you see me when I am taken from you, it is yours; but if not, it is not.”
2.11: And it came to be, as they continued on and spoke, that see, a chariot of fire with horses of fire which separated the two of them. And Ĕliyahu went up by a whirlwind into the shamayim.
2.12: And Elisha saw it, and he cried out, “My father, my father, the chariot of Yisra’ĕl and its horsemen!” And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own garments and tore them into two pieces.
2.13: And he took up the mantle of Ĕliyahu that had fallen from him, and went back and stood by the bank of the Yardĕn.
2.14: And he took the mantle of Ĕliyahu that had fallen from him, and struck the water, and said, “Where is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Ĕliyahu?” And he struck the water, and it was divided this way and that, and Elisha passed over.
2.15: And when the sons of the neḇi’im who were from Yeriḥo saw him, they said, “The spirit of Ĕliyahu rests on Elisha.” And they came to meet him, and bowed to the ground before him.
2.16: And they said to him, “Look, there are fifty strong men with your servants. Please let them go and search for your master, lest the Ruaḥ of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has taken him up and cast him upon some mountain or into some valley.” And he said, “Send no one.”
2.17: But they pressed upon him till he was ashamed, and he said, “Send.” So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days but did not find him.
2.18: And they returned to him, for he remained in Yeriḥo, and he said to them, “Did I not say to you, ‘Do not go’?”
2.19: And the men of the city said to Elisha, “Look, the site of this city is good, as my master sees, but the waters are spoilt, and the land barren.”
2.20: And he said, “Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it.” And they brought it to him.
2.21: And he went out to the source of the water, and threw salt in there, and said, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘I have healed this water - no longer shall death or barrenness come from it.’ ”
2.22: And the waters were healed, to this day, according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.
2.23: And he went up from there to Bĕyth Ĕl. And as he was going up the way, some youths came from the city and mocked him, and said to him, “Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!”
2.24: And he turned around and looked at them, and pronounced a curse on them in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And two female bears came out of the forest and tore to pieces forty-two of the youths.
2.25: And from there he went to Mount Karmel, and from there he returned to Shomeron.

20.1: In those days Ḥizqiyahu was sick unto death. And Yeshayahu the naḇi, son of Amots, went to him and said to him, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Put your house in order, for you are going to die, and not live.’ ”
20.2: And he turned his face toward the wall, and prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
20.3: “I pray to You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done what was good in Your eyes.” And Ḥizqiyahu wept bitterly.
20.4: And it came to be, before Yeshayahu had gone out into the middle court, that the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to him, saying,
20.5: “Return and say to Ḥizqiyahu the leader of My people, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Dawiḏ your father, “I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears. See, I am going to heal you. On the third day go up to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
20.6: “And I shall add to your days fifteen years, and deliver you and this city from the hand of the meleḵ of Ashshur, and shall defend this city for My own sake, and for the sake of Dawiḏ My servant.” ’ ”
20.7: And Yeshayahu said, “Take a cake of figs.” And they took and laid it on the boil, and he recovered.
20.8: And Ḥizqiyahu said to Yeshayahu, “What is the sign that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heals me, and that I shall go up to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the third day?”
20.9: And Yeshayahu said, “This is the sign for you from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does the word which He has spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten degrees or go backward ten degrees?”
20.10: And Ḥizqiyahu said, “It would be easy for the shadow to go down ten degrees; no, but let the shadow go backward ten degrees.”
20.11: And Yeshayahu the naḇi cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down on the sundial of Aḥaz.
20.12: At that time Beroḏaḵ-Balaḏan son of Balaḏan, meleḵ of Baḇel, sent letters and a present to Ḥizqiyahu, for he heard that Ḥizqiyahu had been sick.
20.13: And Ḥizqiyahu listened to them, and showed them all his treasure house, the silver and the gold, and the spices and the precious ointment, and all his armory, and all that was found among his treasures. There was not an object in his house or in all his rule that Ḥizqiyahu did not show them.
20.14: And Yeshayahu the naḇi came to Meleḵ Ḥizqiyahu, and said to him, “What did these men say, and from where did they come to you?” And Ḥizqiyahu said, “They came from a distant land, from Baḇel.”
20.15: And he said, “What have they seen in your house?” And Ḥizqiyahu answered, “They saw all that is in my house; there is not an object among my treasures that I did not show them.”
20.16: And Yeshayahu said to Ḥizqiyahu, “Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄:
20.17: ‘See, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and what your fathers have treasured up until this day, shall be brought to Baḇel - no object is to be left,’ said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
20.18: ‘And they are going to take away some of your sons who are to be born to you, whom you bring forth, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the meleḵ of Baḇel.’ ”
20.19: And Ḥizqiyahu said to Yeshayahu, “The word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which you have spoken is good!” And he said, “Is it not so, if peace and truth are to be in my days?”
20.20: And the rest of the acts of Ḥizqiyahu, and all his might and how he made a pool and a channel and brought water into the city, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
20.21: So Ḥizqiyahu slept with his fathers. And Menashsheh his son reigned in his place.

21.1: Menashsheh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Ḥephtsiḇah.
21.2: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to the abominations of the gentiles whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 dispossessed before the children of Yisra’ĕl.
21.3: For he turned and built the high places which Ḥizqiyahu his father had destroyed, and raised up altars for Ba’al, and made an Ashĕrah, as Aḥaḇ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl had done, and he bowed himself to all the host of the shamayim and served them.
21.4: And he built altars in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said, “In Yerushalayim I put My Name.”
21.5: And he built altars for all the host of the shamayim in the two courtyards of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.6: And he made his son pass through the fire, and practiced magic, and used divination, and consulted spiritists and mediums. He did much evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to provoke.
21.7: And he placed a carved image of Ashĕrah that he had made in the House of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said to Dawiḏ and to Shelomoh his son, “In this House and in Yerushalayim, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, I put My Name forever,
21.8: and no more shall I cause the feet of Yisra’ĕl to move from the land which I gave their fathers - only if they guard to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the Torah that My servant Mosheh commanded them.”
21.9: But they did not obey, and Menashsheh led them astray to do more evil than the gentiles whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had destroyed before the children of Yisra’ĕl.
21.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke by His servants the neḇi’im, saying,
21.11: “Because Menashsheh meleḵ of Yahuḏah has done these abominations, having done more evil than all the Amorites who were before him, and also made Yahuḏah sin with his idols,
21.12: therefore thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘See, I am bringing such evil upon Yerushalayim and Yahuḏah that both ears of those who hear of it shall tingle.
21.13: ‘And I shall stretch over Yerushalayim the measuring line of Shomeron and the plummet of the house of Aḥaḇ, and shall wipe Yerushalayim as one wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down.
21.14: ‘And I shall forsake the remnant of My inheritance and give them into the hand of their enemies. And they shall be for a prey and for a plunder to all their enemies,
21.15: because they have done evil in My eyes, and have provoked Me since the day their fathers came out of Mitsrayim, even to this day.’ ”
21.16: And also, Menashsheh shed very much innocent blood, until he had filled Yerushalayim from one end to another, besides his sin with which he made Yahuḏah sin, in doing evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.17: And the rest of the acts of Menashsheh, and all that he did, and the sin that he committed, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
21.18: So Menashsheh slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza. And his son Amon reigned in his place.
21.19: Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Yerushalayim. And the name of his mother was Meshullemeth the daughter of Ḥaruts of Yoteḇah.
21.20: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as his father Menashsheh had done,
21.21: and walked in all the ways that his father had walked, and served the idols that his father had served, and bowed himself to them,
21.22: and forsook 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of his fathers, and did not walk in the Way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.23: And the servants of Amon conspired against him, and killed the meleḵ in his own house.
21.24: But the people of the land smote all those who had conspired against Meleḵ Amon, and the people of the land appointed his son Yoshiyahu to reign in his place.
21.25: And the rest of the acts of Amon which he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
21.26: And he was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza. And his son Yoshiyahu reigned in his place.

22.1: Yoshiyahu was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeḏiḏah the daughter of Aḏayah of Botsqath.
22.2: And he did what was right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and walked in all the ways of his father Dawiḏ, and did not turn aside, right or left.
22.3: And it came to be, in the eighteenth year of Meleḵ Yoshiyahu, that the meleḵ sent Shaphan the scribe, son of Atsalyahu, son of Meshullam, to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying,
22.4: “Go up to Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn ha’gadol, and let him weigh the silver which has been brought into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which the doorkeepers have gathered from the people.
22.5: “And let them give it into the hand of those doing the work, who are the overseers in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And let them give it to those who are in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 doing the work, to repair the damages of the house,
22.6: to carpenters and to builders and to stonemasons, and to buy timber and hewn stone to repair the house.
22.7: “However, let not the silver given into their hand be reckoned with them, for they are acting trustworthily.”
22.8: And Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn ha’gadol said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the Book of the Torah in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” And Ḥilqiyahu gave the Book to Shaphan, and he read it.
22.9: And Shaphan the scribe came to the meleḵ, and brought word to the meleḵ again, saying, “Your servants have gathered the silver that was found in the house, and have given it into the hand of those who do the work, who oversee the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
22.10: And Shaphan the scribe informed the meleḵ, saying, “Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn has given me a Book.” And Shaphan read it before the meleḵ.
22.11: And it came to be, when the meleḵ heard the words of the Book of the Torah, that he tore his garments,
22.12: and the meleḵ commanded Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn, and Aḥiqam son of Shaphan, and Aḵbor son of Miḵayah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asayah a servant of the meleḵ, saying,
22.13: “Go, inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for me, for the people and for all Yahuḏah, concerning the words of this Book that has been found. For great is the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not obeyed the words of this Book, to do according to all that is written concerning us.”
22.14: Then Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn, and Aḥiqam, and Aḵbor, and Shaphan, and Asayah went to Ḥuldah the neḇiyah, the wife of Shallum son of Tiqwah, son of Ḥarḥas, keeper of the wardrobe. Now she was dwelling in Yerushalayim in the Second Quarter. And they spoke with her.
22.15: And she said to them, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Say to the man who sent you to Me,
22.16: “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘See, I am bringing evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the words of the Book which the meleḵ of Yahuḏah has read,
22.17: because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other mighty ones to provoke Me with all the works of their hands. And so My wrath shall be kindled against this place and not be quenched.’ ” ’
22.18: “And to the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, who sent you to inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, say this to him, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, “As for the words which you have heard,
22.19: because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they would become a ruin and a curse, and tore your garments and wept before Me, I also have heard,” declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.20: “Therefore, see, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, so that your eyes do not see all the evil I am bringing on this place.” ’ ” And they brought word to the meleḵ.

23.1: And the meleḵ sent, and they gathered all the elders of Yahuḏah and Yerushalayim to him.
23.2: And the meleḵ went up to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all the men of Yahuḏah, and all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim with him, and the kohenim and the neḇi’im and all the people, both small and great. And he read in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant which had been found in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.3: And the meleḵ stood by the column and made a covenant before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and to guard His Commands and His Witnesses and His Laws, with all his heart and all his being, to establish the Words of this Covenant that were written in this Book. And all the people stood to the Covenant.
23.4: Then the meleḵ commanded Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn ha’gadol, and the kohenim of the second order, and the doorkeepers, to bring out of the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all the objects that were made for Ba’al, and for Ashĕrah, and for all the host of the shamayim. And he burned them outside Yerushalayim in the fields of Qiḏron, and took their ashes to Bĕyth Ĕl.
23.5: And he put down the black-robed priests whom the melaḵim of Yahuḏah had appointed to burn incense on the high places in the cities of Yahuḏah and in the places all around Yerushalayim, and those who burned incense to Ba’al, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the constellations, and to all the host of the shamayim.
23.6: And he brought out the Ashĕrah from the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to the wadi Qiḏron outside Yerushalayim, and burned it at the wadi Qiḏron and ground it to ashes, and threw its ashes on the graves of the sons of the people.
23.7: And he broke down the houses of the male cult prostitutes that were in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, where the women wove tapestries for the Ashĕrah.
23.8: And he brought all the kohenim from the cities of Yahuḏah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geḇa to Be’ĕrsheḇa, and broke down the high places at the gates which were at the entrance of the Gate of Yahoshua the governor of the city, which were to the left of the city gate.
23.9: However, the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Yerushalayim, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
23.10: And he defiled Topheth, which is in the Valley of Bĕn Hinnom, so that no man could make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Moleḵ.
23.11: And he did away with the horses that the melaḵim of Yahuḏah had given to the sun, at the entrance to the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, by the room of Nathan-Meleḵ the eunuch, that were in the court. And he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.
23.12: And the altars that were on the roof of the upper room of Aḥaz, which the melaḵim of Yahuḏah had made, and the altars which Menashsheh had made in the two courtyards of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the meleḵ broke down, and rushed from there, and threw their dust into the wadi Qiḏron.
23.13: And the meleḵ defiled the high places that were before Yerushalayim, which were on the right hand of the Mountain of Destruction, which Shelomoh meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Tsiḏonians, and for Kemosh the abomination of the Mo’aḇites, and for Milkom the abomination of the children of Ammon.
23.14: And he broke in pieces the pillars and cut down the Ashĕrim, and filled their places with the bones of men.
23.15: And also the altar that was at Bĕyth Ĕl, and the high place which Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat made, by which he made Yisra’ĕl sin, both that altar and the high place he broke down. And he burned the high place and ground it to dust, and burned the Ashĕrah.
23.16: Then Yoshiyahu turned, and saw the tombs that were there on the mountain. And he sent and took the bones out of the tombs and burned them on the altar, and defiled it according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which the man of Elohim proclaimed, who proclaimed these words.
23.17: And he said, “What tombstone is this that I see?” And the men of the city said to him, “It is the tomb of the man of Elohim who came from Yahuḏah and proclaimed these matters which you have done against the altar of Bĕyth Ĕl.”
23.18: And he said, “Let him alone, let no one move his bones.” So they left his bones alone, with the bones of the naḇi who came from Shomeron.
23.19: And Yoshiyahu also took away all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Shomeron, which the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl had made to provoke. And he did to them according to all the deeds he did in Bĕyth Ĕl.
23.20: And he slaughtered all the priests of the high places who were there, on the altars, and burned men’s bones on them, and went back to Yerushalayim.
23.21: And the meleḵ commanded all the people, saying, “Prepare the Pesaḥ to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant.”
23.22: For such a Pesaḥ had not been prepared since the days of the rulers who ruled Yisra’ĕl, nor in all the days of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl and the melaḵim of Yahuḏah,
23.23: but in the eighteenth year of Meleḵ Yoshiyahu this Pesaḥ was prepared before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in Yerushalayim.
23.24: And also, Yoshiyahu put away those who consulted mediums and spiritists, and the household mighty ones and idols, and all the abominations that were seen in the land of Yahuḏah and in Yerushalayim, in order to establish the words of the Torah which were written in the Book that Ḥilqiyahu the kohĕn found in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.25: And before him there was no meleḵ like him, who turned back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all his heart, and with all his being, and with all his might, according to all the Torah of Mosheh; and after him none rose up like him.
23.26: However, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 did not turn from the fierceness of His great wrath, with which His wrath burned against Yahuḏah, because of all the provocations with which Menashsheh had provoked Him.
23.27: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, “Even Yahuḏah I shall remove from My presence, as I have removed Yisra’ĕl, and I shall reject this city Yerushalayim which I have chosen, and the House of which I said, ‘My Name is there.’ ”
23.28: And the rest of the acts of Yoshiyahu, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
23.29: In his days Pharaoh Neḵo meleḵ of Mitsrayim went up against the meleḵ of Ashshur, to the River Perath. And Meleḵ Yoshiyahu went out to him, and he killed him at Meḡiddo when he saw him.
23.30: And his servants conveyed his body in a chariot from Meḡiddo, and brought him to Yerushalayim, and buried him in his own tomb. And the people of the land took Yaho’aḥaz son of Yoshiyahu, and anointed him, and appointed him to reign in his father’s place.
23.31: Yaho’aḥaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Ḥamutal the daughter of Yirmeyahu of Liḇnah.
23.32: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that his fathers did.
23.33: And Pharaoh Neḵo imprisoned him at Riḇlah in the land of Ḥamath, to keep him from reigning in Yerushalayim. And he imposed on the land a fine of one hundred kiḵars of silver and a kiḵar of gold.
23.34: And Pharaoh Neḵo appointed Elyaqim son of Yoshiyahu to reign in place of his father Yoshiyahu, and changed his name to Yahoyaqim. And Pharaoh took Yaho’aḥaz and went to Mitsrayim, and he died there.
23.35: And Yahoyaqim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh. Only, he taxed the land to give silver according to the command of Pharaoh. He exacted the silver and gold from the people of the land, from every one according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Neḵo.
23.36: Yahoyaqim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Zeḇiḏah the daughter of Peḏayah of Rumah.
23.37: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that his fathers did.

24.1: In his days Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel came up, and Yahoyaqim became his servant for three years. And he turned and rebelled against him.
24.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent against him raiding bands of Kasdites, and raiding bands of Aram, and raiding bands of Mo’aḇ, and raiding bands of the children of Ammon. And He sent them against Yahuḏah to destroy it, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He had spoken by His servants the neḇi’im.
24.3: Only at the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 this came upon Yahuḏah, to remove from His presence, because of the sins of Menashsheh, according to all that he did,
24.4: and also because of the innocent blood that he shed. For he filled Yerushalayim with innocent blood, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would not forgive.
24.5: And the rest of the acts of Yahoyaqim, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
24.6: So Yahoyaqim slept with his fathers. And Yahoyaḵin his son reigned in his place.
24.7: And the meleḵ of Mitsrayim did not come out of his land again, for the meleḵ of Baḇel had taken all that belonged to the meleḵ of Mitsrayim from the wadi of Mitsrayim to the River Perath.
24.8: Yahoyaḵin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Yerushalayim three months. And his mother’s name was Neḥushta the daughter of Elnathan of Yerushalayim.
24.9: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that his father did.
24.10: At that time the servants of Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel came up against Yerushalayim, and the city was besieged.
24.11: And Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel came against the city, as his servants were besieging it.
24.12: And Yahoyaḵin meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and his mother, and his servants, and his heads, and his eunuchs went out to the meleḵ of Baḇel. And the meleḵ of Baḇel, in the eighth year of his reign, took him prisoner.
24.13: And he took from there all the treasures of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the treasures of the meleḵ’s house, and he cut in pieces all the objects of gold which Shelomoh meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl had made in the Hĕyḵal of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said.
