24.14: And he exiled all Yerushalayim, and all the officers and all the mighty brave men - ten thousand exiles - and all the craftsmen and smiths. None remained except the poorest people of the land.
24.15: And he exiled Yahoyaḵin to Baḇel. And the meleḵ’s mother, and the meleḵ’s wives, and his eunuchs, and the leading men of the land he exiled from Yerushalayim to Baḇel.
24.16: And all the mighty brave men, seven thousand, and craftsmen and smiths, one thousand, all who were strong and fit for battle, these the meleḵ of Baḇel brought to Baḇel into exile.
24.17: And the meleḵ of Baḇel appointed Mattanyah, Yahoyaḵin’s uncle, to reign in his place, and changed his name to Tsiḏqiyahu.
24.18: Tsiḏqiyahu was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Ḥamutal the daughter of Yirmeyahu of Liḇnah.
24.19: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, according to all that Yahoyaqim did.
24.20: For this took place in Yerushalayim and Yahuḏah because of the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, until He had cast them out from His presence. And Tsiḏqiyahu rebelled against the meleḵ of Baḇel.

25.1: And it came to be in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, that Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel and all his army came against Yerushalayim and encamped against it, and they built a siege wall against it all around.
25.2: And the city was besieged until the eleventh year of Meleḵ Tsiḏqiyahu.
25.3: By the ninth of the month the scarcity of food had become so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land.
25.4: Then the city wall was breached, and all the men of battle fled at night by way of the gate between two walls, which was by the meleḵ’s garden, even though the Kasdites were still encamped all around against the city. And the meleḵ went by way of the desert plain.
25.5: And the army of the Kasdites pursued the meleḵ, and overtook him in the desert plains of Yeriḥo, and all his army was scattered from him.
25.6: And they seized the meleḵ and brought him up to the meleḵ of Baḇel at Riḇlah, and they pronounced sentence on him.
25.7: And they slaughtered the sons of Tsiḏqiyahu before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Tsiḏqiyahu, and bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Baḇel.
25.8: And in the fifth month, on the seventh of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Meleḵ Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel, Neḇuzaraḏan the chief of the guard, a servant of the meleḵ of Baḇel, came to Yerushalayim.
25.9: And he burned the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the house of the meleḵ, and all the houses of Yerushalayim - even every great house he burned with fire.
25.10: And all the army of the Kasdites who were with the chief of the guard broke down the walls of Yerushalayim all around.
25.11: And Neḇuzaraḏan the chief of the guard took into exile the rest of the people who were left in the city and the deserters who deserted to the meleḵ of Baḇel, with the rest of the multitude.
25.12: But the chief of the guard left some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and farmers.
25.13: And the bronze columns that were in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Kasdites broke in pieces, and took their bronze away to Baḇel.
25.14: And they took the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the ladles, and all the bronze utensils the kohenim used in the service.
25.15: And the chief of the guard took the fire holders and the basins which were of solid gold and solid silver.
25.16: The bronze of all these utensils was beyond measure - the two columns, the one sea, and the stands, which Shelomoh had made for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
25.17: The height of one column was eighteen ammah, and the capital on it was of bronze. And the height of the capital was three ammah, and the network and pomegranates all around the capital were all of bronze. And the second column was the same, with a network.
25.18: And the chief of the guard took Serayah the chief kohĕn, and Tsephanyahu the second kohĕn, and the three doorkeepers.
25.19: And out of the city he took a certain eunuch who was appointed over the men of battle, and five men of those who saw the meleḵ’s face, who were found in the city, and the chief scribe of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
25.20: And Neḇuzaraḏan, chief of the guard, took them and made them go to the meleḵ of Baḇel at Riḇlah.
25.21: And the meleḵ of Baḇel smote them and put them to death at Riḇlah in the land of Ḥamath. So he exiled Yahuḏah from its own land.
25.22: And he appointed Geḏalyahu son of Aḥiqam, son of Shaphan, over the people who were left in the land of Yahuḏah, whom Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar meleḵ of Baḇel had left.
25.23: And all the commanders of the armies, they and their men, heard that the meleḵ of Baḇel had appointed Geḏalyahu. And they came to Geḏalyahu at Mitspah, even Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah, and Yoḥanan son of Qarĕaḥ, and Serayah son of Tanḥumeth the Netophathite, and Ya’azanyahu the son of a Ma’aḵathite, they and their men.
25.24: And Geḏalyahu swore to them and their men, and said to them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Kasdites. Dwell in the land and serve the meleḵ of Baḇel, and let it be well with you.”
25.25: And in the seventh month it came to be that Yishma’ĕl son of Nethanyah, son of Elishama, of the seed of the reign, came with ten men and smote Geḏalyahu that he died, and the Yahuḏim, and the Kasdites who were with him at Mitspah.
25.26: And all the people rose up, small and great, and the commanders of the armies, and went to Mitsrayim, for they were afraid of the Kasdites.
25.27: And it came to be in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Yahoyaḵin meleḵ of Yahuḏah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, that Ewil-Meroḏaḵ meleḵ of Baḇel, in the year that he began to reign, released Yahoyaḵin meleḵ of Yahuḏah from prison,
25.28: and spoke kindly to him, and appointed his throne above the throne of the melaḵim who were with him in Baḇel,
25.29: and changed his prison garments. And he ate bread continually before the meleḵ all the days of his life.
25.30: And as his allowance, a continual allowance was given to him from the meleḵ, a quota for each day, all the days of his life.

3.1: And Yahoram son of Aḥaḇ began to reign over Yisra’ĕl at Shomeron in the eighteenth year of Yahoshaphat meleḵ of Yahuḏah, and reigned twelve years.
3.2: And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but not like his father and mother; for he removed the statue of Ba’al which his father had made.
3.3: But he clung to the sins of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ĕl sin. He did not turn away from them.
3.4: And Mĕysha meleḵ of Mo’aḇ was a sheep-breeder, and he paid the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.
3.5: And it came to be, when Aḥaḇ died, that the meleḵ of Mo’aḇ revolted against the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.
3.6: And Meleḵ Yahoram went out of Shomeron at that time and mustered all Yisra’ĕl.
3.7: And he went and sent to Yahoshaphat meleḵ of Yahuḏah, saying, “The meleḵ of Mo’aḇ has revolted against me. Do you go with me to fight against Mo’aḇ?” And he said, “I go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.”
3.8: And he said, “Which way do we go up?” And he said, “By way of the Wilderness of Eḏom.”
3.9: And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl went, and the meleḵ of Yahuḏah and the meleḵ of Eḏom, and went round a journey of seven days. And there was no water for the army, nor for the cattle that followed them.
3.10: And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl said, “What? Has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 called these three melaḵim to give them into the hand of Mo’aḇ?”
3.11: And Yahoshaphat said, “Is there no naḇi of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 here? Then let us inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 through him.” One of the servants of the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl then answered and said, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water out on the hands of Ĕliyahu.”
3.12: And Yahoshaphat said, “The word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with him.” And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl and Yahoshaphat and the meleḵ of Eḏom went down to him.
3.13: And Elisha said to the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, “What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and the prophets of your mother.” And the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl said to him, “No, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has called these three melaḵim to give them into the hand of Mo’aḇ.”
3.14: And Elisha said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts lives, before whom I stand, if it were not that I regard the presence of Yahoshaphat meleḵ of Yahuḏah, I would not look at you nor see you.
3.15: “And now, bring me a harpist.” And it came to be, when the harpist played, that the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came upon him.
3.16: And he said, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Make this wadi ditches - ditches.’
3.17: “For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘You are not going to see wind, nor rain. Yet that wadi is to be filled with water, so that you, your cattle, and your beasts shall drink.’
3.18: “And this shall be but a light matter in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And He shall give Mo’aḇ into your hand.
3.19: “And you shall smite every walled city and every choice city, and shall cut down every good tree, and stop up every fountain of water, and ruin every good piece of land with stones.”
3.20: And it came to be in the morning, when the grain offering was offered, that see, water came by way of Eḏom, and the land was filled with water.
3.21: And when all Mo’aḇ heard that the melaḵim had come up to fight against them, all who were able to bear arms and older were gathered, and they stood at the border.
3.22: And they rose up early in the morning, and the sun was shining on the water. And the Mo’aḇites saw the water on the other side as red as blood.
3.23: And they said, “This is blood. The melaḵim have indeed struck swords and have killed one another. And now, Mo’aḇ, to the spoil!”
3.24: And they came to the camp of Yisra’ĕl, and Yisra’ĕl rose up and smote the Mo’aḇites, so that they fled before them. And they entered their land, and smote the Mo’aḇites.
3.25: And they broke down the cities, and each man threw a stone on every good piece of land and filled it. And they stopped up all the fountains of water and cut down all the good trees, until the stones of Qir Ḥaraseth were left. And the slingers went round and smote it.
3.26: And when the meleḵ of Mo’aḇ saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew swords, to break through to the meleḵ of Eḏom, but they could not,
3.27: then took his eldest son who would have reigned in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering upon the wall. And there was great wrath against Yisra’ĕl. And they left him and returned to the land.

4.1: And a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the neḇi’im cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant revered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And the lender has come to take my two sons to be his slaves.”
4.2: And Elisha said to her, “What should I do for you? Inform me, what do you have in the house?” And she said, “Your female servant has none at all in the house except a pot of oil.”
4.3: And he said, “Go, borrow vessels from everywhere, from all your neighbors, empty vessels, do not get a few.
4.4: “And when you have come in, you shall shut the door behind you and your sons. Then pour it into all those vessels, and put aside the filled ones.”
4.5: So she went from him and shut the door behind her and her sons, who brought to her, and she poured it out.
4.6: And it came to be, when the vessels were filled, that she said to her son, “Bring me another vessel.” But he said to her, “There is not another vessel.” And the oil ceased.
4.7: So she went and informed the man of Elohim, and he said, “Go, sell the oil and pay your debt. And you and your sons live on the rest.”
4.8: And it came to be on a day that Elisha went to Shunĕm, where there was a prominent woman, and she urged him to eat some food. And it came to be, as often as he passed by, that he turned in there to eat some food.
4.9: And she said to her husband, “Look, I know that this is a qodesh man of Elohim, who passes by us continually.
4.10: “Please, let us make a small upper room on the wall, and let us put a bed for him there, and a table and a chair and a lampstand. And it shall be, whenever he comes to us, let him turn in there.”
4.11: And it came to be on a day that he came there, and he turned in to the upper room and lay down there.
4.12: And he said to Gĕḥazi his servant, “Call this Shunammite woman.” So he called her, and she stood before him.
4.13: And he said to him, “Please say to her, ‘Look, you have gone to all this trouble for us. What is there to be done for you? Should I speak on your behalf to the meleḵ or to the commander of the army?’ ” And she answered, “I am dwelling among my own people.”
4.14: And he said, “What then is to be done for her?” And Gĕḥazi answered, “Well, she has no son, and her husband is old.”
4.15: And he said, “Call her.” So he called her, and she stood in the doorway.
4.16: And he said, “About this time next year you shall embrace a son.” And she said, “No, my master, man of Elohim, do not lie to your female servant!”
4.17: And the woman conceived, and bore a son when the appointed time had come, of which Elisha had spoken to her.
4.18: And the child grew. And it came to be on a day that he went out to his father, to the reapers,
4.19: and he said to his father, “My head, my head!” And he said to a servant, “Take him to his mother.”
4.20: So he took him and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees till noon, and died.
4.21: And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of Elohim, and shut him in, and went out.
4.22: And she called to her husband, and said, “Please send me one of the young men and one of the donkeys, so that I hurry to the man of Elohim and return.”
4.23: And he said, “Why are you going to him today? It is neither the New Moon nor the Shabbath.” And she said, “It is well!”
4.24: And she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Drive and go, do not slow down, except I speak to you.”
4.25: And she went, and came to the man of Elohim at Mount Karmel. And it came to be, when the man of Elohim saw her at a distance, that he said to his servant Gĕḥazi, “See, the Shunammite woman.
4.26: “Please run now to meet her, and say to her, ‘Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?’ ” And she answered, “It is well.”
4.27: And she came to the man of Elohim at the hill, and she caught him by the feet, but Gĕḥazi came near to push her away. But the man of Elohim said, “Leave her alone, for her being is bitter in her, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has hidden it from me, and has not revealed it to me.”
4.28: And she said, “Did I ask a son of my master? Did I not say, ‘Do not deceive me’?”
4.29: And he said to Gĕḥazi, “Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go. When you meet anyone, do not greet him, and when anyone greets you, do not answer him. And you shall lay my staff on the face of the child.”
4.30: And the mother of the child said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, and as your being lives, I do not leave you.” And he rose and followed her.
4.31: And Gĕḥazi went on ahead of them, and laid the staff on the face of the child. But there was no voice and there was no hearing, so he went back to meet him, and reported to him, saying, “The child has not awakened.”
4.32: And Elisha came into the house and saw the child was dead, lying on his bed,
4.33: and he went in, and shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
4.34: And he went up and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretched himself out on the child, and the flesh of the child became warm.
4.35: And he returned and walked back and forth in the house, then went up and stretched himself out on him. And the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
4.36: And he called Gĕḥazi and said, “Call this Shunammite.” So he called her and she came in to him, and he said, “Pick up your son.”
4.37: Then she went in and fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground, and picked up her son and went out.
4.38: And Elisha returned to Gilgal. And the scarcity of food was in the land, and the sons of the neḇi’im were sitting before him. And he said to his servant, “Put on the large pot, and cook stew for the sons of the neḇi’im.”
4.39: And one went out to the field to gather plants, and found a wild vine, and gathered wild cucumbers from it, filling the skirt of his garment, and came and sliced them into the pot of stew, though they did not know what they were.
4.40: They then served it to the men to eat. And it came to be, as they were eating the stew, that they cried out and said, “O man of Elohim, there is death in the pot!” And they were unable to eat it.
4.41: And he said, “Then bring some flour.” And he put it into the pot, and said, “Serve it to the people to eat.” And there was no evil matter in the pot.
4.42: Now a man came from Ba’al Shalishah, and brought the man of Elohim bread of the first-fruits, twenty loaves of barley bread, and newly ripened grain in his knapsack. And he said, “Give it to the people to eat.”
4.43: And his servant said, “What? Do I put this before one hundred men?” And he said, “Give it to the people to eat. For thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Eat and have some left over.’ ”
4.44: And he put it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

5.1: And Na’aman, commander of the army of the meleḵ of Aram, was a great man in the eyes of his master, and highly respected, because by him 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had given deliverance to Aram. And though a brave man, was leprous.
5.2: And the Arameans had gone out on raids, and had brought back captive a young girl from the land of Yisra’ĕl, and she served the wife of Na’aman.
5.3: And she said to her mistress, “If only my master were with the naḇi who is in Shomeron! Then he would recover him of his leprosy.”
5.4: And Na’aman went in and reported to his master, saying, “Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from the land of Yisra’ĕl.”
5.5: And the meleḵ of Aram said, “Go, enter, and let me send a letter to the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.” And he went and took with him ten kiḵars of silver, and six thousand gold, and ten changes of garments.
5.6: And he brought the letter to the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, which said, “And now, when this letter comes to you, see I have sent Na’aman my servant to you, so that you shall recover him of his leprosy.”
5.7: And it came to be, when the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl read the letter, that he tore his garments and said, “Am I Elohim, to kill and keep alive, that this man sends a man to me to recover him of his leprosy? For consider now, and see how he is seeking an occasion with me!”
5.8: And it came to be, when Elisha the man of Elohim heard that the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl had torn his garments, that he sent to meleḵ, saying, “Why have you torn your garments? Please let him come to me, so that he knows that there is a naḇi in Yisra’ĕl.”
5.9: So Na’aman came with his horses and chariot, and he stood at the entrance of the house of Elisha.
5.10: And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go, and you shall wash seven times in the Yardĕn, that your flesh might be restored to you, and be clean.”
5.11: But Na’aman became wroth, and went away and said, “See, I said to myself, ‘He would certainly come out to me, and stand and call on the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim, and wave his hand over the place, and recover, the leprosy.’
5.12: “Are not the Aḇanah and the Pharpar, the rivers of Dammeseq, better than all the waters of Yisra’ĕl? Could I not wash in them and be clean?” And he turned and went away in a rage.
5.13: And his servants came near and spoke to him, and said, “My father, if the naḇi had spoken to you a great matter, would you not have done it? How much more then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean’?”
5.14: Then he went down and dipped seven times in the Yardĕn, according to the word of the man of Elohim. And his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
5.15: And he returned to the man of Elohim, he and all his company, and came and stood before him and said, “See, now I know that there is no Elohim in all the earth, except in Yisra’ĕl. And now, please take a gift from your servant.”
5.16: But he said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, before whom I stand, I do not accept it.” And he pressed on him to accept it, but he refused.
5.17: Then Na’aman said, “If not, please let your servant be given two mule-loads of earth, for no longer is your servant going to make a burnt offering and slaughtering to other mighty ones, but to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
5.18: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 grant forgiveness to your servant in this matter: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon; when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, please grant forgiveness to your servant in this matter.”
5.19: Then he said to him, “Go in peace.” And he walked from him some distance.
5.20: But Gĕḥazi, the servant of Elisha the man of Elohim, said, “Look, my master has spared Na’aman this Aramean, while not receiving from his hands what he brought. But as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lives, I shall run after him and take whatever from him.”
5.21: And Gĕḥazi pursued Na’aman. And when Na’aman saw him running after him, he came down from the chariot to meet him, and said, “Is there peace?”
5.22: And he said, “Peace. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Look, even now two young men of the sons of the neḇi’im have come to me from the mountains of Ephrayim. Please give them a kiḵar of silver and two changes of garments.’ ”
5.23: And Na’aman said, “Please accept two kiḵars.” And he urged him, and bound two kiḵars of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and handed them to two of his servants. And they bore them ahead of him.
5.24: And when he came to the high place, he took them from their hand, and stored them away in the house, and let the men go, and they went.
5.25: And he went in and stood before his master, and Elisha said to him, “Where did you go, Gĕḥazi?” And he said, “Your servant did not go anywhere.”
5.26: But he said to him, “Did not my heart go with you when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Is it time to accept silver and to accept garments, and olive trees and vineyards, and sheep and cattle, and male and female servants?
5.27: “So let the leprosy of Na’aman cling to you and your descendants forever.” And he went out from him as leprous as snow.

6.1: And the sons of the neḇi’im said to Elisha, “See, the place where we dwell with you is too small for us.
6.2: “Please, let us go to the Yardĕn, and let every man take a log from there, and let us make there a place to dwell.” And he answered, “Go.”
6.3: Then the one said, “Please undertake to go with your servants.” And he answered, “I shall go.”
6.4: And he went with them, and they came to the Yardĕn, and they cut down trees.
6.5: And it came to be, as one was cutting down a tree, that the iron axe head fell into the water. And he cried out and said, “Oh my master!” For it was borrowed.
6.6: And the man of Elohim said, “Where did it fall?” And he showed him the place. And he cut off a stick, and threw it in there, and made the iron float.
6.7: And he said, “Pick it up.” And he reached out his hand and took it.
6.8: And the meleḵ of Aram was fighting against Yisra’ĕl, and took counsel with his servants, saying, “My camp is in such and such a place.”
6.9: And the man of Elohim sent to the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “Be on guard, do not pass this place, for the Arameans are coming down there.”
6.10: The meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl then sent to the place of which the man of Elohim had spoken to him, and warned him, so that he was on his guard there, not once, and not twice.
6.11: And this greatly troubled the heart of the meleḵ of Aram. And he called his servants and said to them, “Declare to me! Who of us is for the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl?”
6.12: And one of his servants said, “None, my master, O meleḵ, for Elisha, the naḇi who is in Yisra’ĕl, declares to the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl the words that you speak in your bedroom.”
6.13: And he said, “Go and see where he is, so that I send and get him.” And it was reported to him, saying, “See, he is in Dothan.”
6.14: And he sent horses and chariots and a great army there, and they came by night and surrounded the city.
6.15: And the servant of the man of Elohim rose early and went out, and saw an army, surrounding the city with horses and chariots. And his servant said to him, “Oh, my master! What do we do?”
6.16: And he answered, “Do not fear, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”
6.17: And Elisha prayed, and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I pray, open his eyes and let him see.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 opened the eyes of the young man, and he looked and saw the mountain covered with horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
6.18: And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and said, “Strike this nation with blindness, I pray.” And He struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
6.19: And Elisha said to them, “This is not the way, nor is this the city. Follow me, and let me bring you to the man whom you seek.” But he led them to Shomeron.
6.20: And it came to be, when they had come to Shomeron, that Elisha said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, open the eyes of these men so that they see.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 opened their eyes, and they looked and saw they were in the midst of Shomeron!
6.21: And when the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl saw them, he said to Elisha, “My father, should I smite? Should I smite?”
6.22: But he said, “Do not smite. Do you smite those whom you have taken captive with your sword and your bow? Put food and water before them and let them eat and drink and go to their master.”
6.23: And he made a great feast for them. And after they ate and drank, he let them go, and they went to their master. And the bands of Aramean raiders came no more into the land of Yisra’ĕl.
6.24: And after this it came to be that Ben-Haḏaḏ the meleḵ of Aram mustered all his army, and went up and besieged Shomeron.
6.25: And there was a great scarcity of food in Shomeron. And see, they besieged it until a donkey’s head went at eighty pieces of silver, and one-fourth of a kab of dove droppings for five pieces of silver.
6.26: And it came to be, as the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, saying, “Help, my master, O meleḵ!”
6.27: And he said, “If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does not help you, where do I find help for you? From the threshing-floor or from the winepress?”
6.28: And the meleḵ said to her, “What is troubling you?” And she answered, “This woman said to me, ‘Give your son and let us eat him today, and tomorrow we eat my son.’
6.29: “So we cooked my son, and ate him. And I said to her on the next day, ‘Give your son and let us eat him.’ But she has hidden her son.”
6.30: And it came to be, when the meleḵ heard the words of the woman, that he tore his garments. And as he passed by on the wall, the people looked and saw the sackcloth on his body, underneath.
6.31: And he said, “Elohim do so to me and more also, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today.”
6.32: And Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. And he sent a man ahead of him, but before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, “Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent someone to take away my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door, and hold him fast at the door. Is not the sound of his master’s feet behind him?”
6.33: While he was still speaking with them, then see, the messenger came down to him, and he said, “Look, this evil is from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, why should I wait for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 any longer?”

7.1: And Elisha said, “Hear the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘About this time tomorrow a se’ah of fine flour for a sheqel, and two se’im of barley for a sheqel, at the gate of Shomeron.’ ”
7.2: And an officer on whose hand the meleḵ leaned answered the man of Elohim and said, “Look, if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is making windows in the shamayim, shall this word come true?” And he said, “Look, you are about to see it with your eyes, but not eat of it.”
7.3: And there were four leprous men at the entrance of the gate. And they said to each other, “Why are we sitting here until we are dead?
7.4: “If we shall say, ‘Let us go into the city,’ the scarcity of food is in the city, and we shall die there. And if we sit here, we shall die. And now, come, let us surrender to the army of the Arameans. If they keep us alive, we live. And if they kill us, we shall die.”
7.5: So at twilight they rose up to go to the camp of the Arameans. And when they had come to the outskirts of the Aramean camp, look, no one was there.
7.6: For Aḏonai had caused the army of the Arameans to hear the noise of chariots and the noise of horses, the noise of a great army, and they said to each other, “Look, the meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl has hired against us the melaḵim of the Ḥittites and the melaḵim of the Mitsrites to come against us!”
7.7: So they rose up and fled at twilight, and left the camp as it is - their tents, and their horses, and their donkeys - and they fled for their lives.
7.8: And when these lepers came to the outskirts of the camp, they went into one tent and ate and drank, and took from there silver and gold and garments, and went and hid them. And they came back and went into another tent, and took from there and went and hid it.
7.9: Then they said to each other, “We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. And if we wait until morning light, then wickedness shall come upon us. And now, come, let us go and inform the house of the meleḵ.”
7.10: And they came and called to the gatekeepers of the city, and informed them, saying, “We went to the camp of Aram, and look, there is not a man or a voice of man, only horses tied and donkeys tied, and the tents as they were.”
7.11: And the gatekeepers called, and they informed the house of the meleḵ inside.
7.12: So the meleḵ rose up in the night and said to his servants, “Let me now inform you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are starving, so they have gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, ‘When they come out of the city, we shall catch them alive, and enter into the city.’ ”
7.13: And one of his servants answered and said, “Please, let some take five of the horses that are left in the city. Look, they are like the entire crowd of Yisra’ĕl that are left in it, look, they are like the entire crowd of Yisra’ĕl left from those who are consumed. So let us send and see.”
7.14: They then took two chariots with horses. And the meleḵ sent them in the direction of the camp of Aram, saying, “Go and see.”
7.15: And they went after them to the Yardĕn. And look, all the way was littered with garments and weapons which the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. And the messengers returned and reported to the meleḵ.
7.16: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of Aram. So a se’ah of fine flour was for a sheqel, and two se’im of barley for a sheqel, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
7.17: And the meleḵ had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned to be in charge of the gate. But the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, as the man of Elohim had said, who spoke when the meleḵ came down to him.
7.18: And it came to be, as the man of Elohim had spoken to the meleḵ, saying, “Two se’im of barley for a sheqel, and a se’ah of fine flour for a sheqel, at this time tomorrow in the gate of Shomeron,”
7.19: that officer answered the man of Elohim, and said, “Now look, if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is making windows in the shamayim, is it according to this word?” And he had said, “Look, you are about to see it with your eyes, but not eat of it.”
7.20: And so it came to be for him, for the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

8.1: And Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Rise up and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you do sojourn, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has called for a scarcity of food, and also, it is coming upon the land for seven years.”
8.2: And the woman rose up and did according to the word of the man of Elohim, and she went with her household and sojourned in the land of the Pelishtites, seven years.
8.3: And it came to be, at the end of seven years, that the woman returned from the land of the Pelishtites. And she went to cry out to the meleḵ for her house and for her land.
8.4: And the meleḵ was speaking to Gĕḥazi, the servant of the man of Elohim, saying, “Please relate to me all the great matters Elisha has done.”
8.5: And it came to be, as he was relating to the meleḵ how he had restored the dead to life, that see, the woman whose son he had restored to life, was crying out to the meleḵ for her house and for her land. And Gĕḥazi said, “My master, O meleḵ, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life.”
8.6: So the meleḵ asked the woman, and she related to him. And the meleḵ appointed a certain eunuch for her, saying, “Return all that was hers, and all the increase of the field from the day that she left the land until now.”
8.7: And Elisha came to Dammeseq, and Ben-Haḏaḏ meleḵ of Aram was sick. And it was reported to him, saying, “The man of Elohim has come here.”
8.8: And the meleḵ said to Ḥaza’ĕl, “Take a present in your hand, and go to meet the man of Elohim, and inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by him, saying, ‘Do I recover from this sickness?’ ”
8.9: And Ḥaza’ĕl went to meet him and took a present with him, of all the goods of Dammeseq, forty camel-loads. And he came and stood before him, and said, “Your son Ben-Haḏaḏ meleḵ of Aram has sent me to you, saying, ‘Do I recover from this sickness?’ ”
8.10: And Elisha said to him, “Go, say to him, ‘You shall certainly recover.’ But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has shown me that he shall certainly die.”
8.11: And he looked steadily until he was ashamed. Then the man of Elohim wept.
8.12: And Ḥaza’ĕl said, “Why is my master weeping?” And he answered, “Because I know the evil that you are going to do to the children of Yisra’ĕl: Lighting their strongholds on fire, and slaying their young men with the sword, and dashing their children, and ripping open their women with child.”
8.13: And Ḥaza’ĕl said, “But what is your servant - a dog, that he should perform this great matter?” And Elisha answered, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has shown that you are to be meleḵ over Aram!”
8.14: And he left Elisha, and came to his master, who said to him, “What did Elisha say to you?” And he answered, “He said to me that you shall certainly recover.”
8.15: And on the next day it came to be that he took a thick cloth and dipped it in water, and spread it over his face so that he died. And Ḥaza’ĕl reigned in his place.
8.16: And in the fifth year of Yahoram son of Aḥaḇ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl - Yahoshaphat was meleḵ of Yahuḏah - Yahoram son of Yahoshaphat began to reign as meleḵ of Yahuḏah.
8.17: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Yerushalayim.
8.18: And he walked in the way of the melaḵim of Yisra’ĕl, as the house of Aḥaḇ had done, for the daughter of Aḥaḇ was his wife. And he did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.19: However, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would not destroy Yahuḏah, for the sake of Dawiḏ His servant, as He promised him to give a lamp to him and his sons forever.
8.20: In his days Eḏom revolted from under the hand of Yahuḏah, and made a meleḵ over themselves.
8.21: And Yoram passed over to Tsa’ir, and all his chariots with him. And he rose by night and smote the Eḏomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots, but his people fled to their tents.
8.22: Yet Eḏom has been in revolt from under the hand of Yahuḏah to this day. Then Liḇnah revolted at the same time.
8.23: And the rest of the acts of Yoram, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the melaḵim of Yahuḏah?
8.24: So Yoram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Dawiḏ. And Aḥazyahu his son reigned in his place.
8.25: In the twelfth year of Yoram son of Aḥaḇ meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, Aḥazyahu son of Yahoram meleḵ of Yahuḏah began to reign.
8.26: Aḥazyahu was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Yerushalayim. And the name of his mother was Athalyahu, the granddaughter of Omri, meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl.
8.27: And he walked in the way of the house of Aḥaḇ, and did evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as the house of Aḥaḇ had done, for he was the son-in-law of the house of Aḥaḇ.
8.28: And he went with Yoram son of Aḥaḇ to battle against Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram at Ramoth Gil’aḏ, and the Arameans struck Yoram.
8.29: And Meleḵ Yoram went back to Yizre’ĕl to recover from the wounds with which the Arameans had struck him at Ramah, when he fought against Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram. Then Aḥazyahu son of Yahoram, the meleḵ of Yahuḏah, went down to see Yoram son of Aḥaḇ in Yizre’ĕl, for he was sick.

9.1: And Elisha the naḇi called one of the sons of the neḇi’im, and said to him, “Gird your loins and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth Gil’aḏ.
9.2: “And you shall go there and look there for Yahu son of Yahoshaphat, son of Nimshi, and go in and make him rise up from among his brothers, and take him to an inner room,
9.3: “and take the flask of oil, and pour it on his head, and say, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I have anointed you meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl.” ’ Then you shall open the door and flee, and do not wait.”
9.4: So the young man - the young man the naḇi - went to Ramoth Gil’aḏ,
9.5: and came in and saw the commanders of the army sitting. And he said, “I have a message for you, O commander.” And Yahu said, “For which one of us?” And he said, “For you, commander.”
9.6: And he rose up and went into the house. And he poured the oil on his head, and said to him, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, ‘I anointed you meleḵ over people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, over Yisra’ĕl.
9.7: ‘And you shall smite the house of Aḥaḇ your master, and I shall avenge the blood of My servants the neḇi’im, and the blood of all the servants of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, at the hand of Izeḇel.
9.8: ‘And all the house of Aḥaḇ shall perish. And I shall cut off from Aḥaḇ all the males in Yisra’ĕl, both those shut up and those left at large.
9.9: ‘And I shall give up the house of Aḥaḇ like the house of Yaroḇ’am son of Neḇat, and like the house of Ba’asha son of Aḥiyahu.
9.10: ‘And the dogs are going to eat Izeḇel in the portion of Yizre’ĕl, with none to bury her.’ ” Then he opened the door and fled.
9.11: And Yahu came out to the servants of his master, and one said to him, “Is there peace? Why did this madman come to you?” And he said to them, “You know the man and his talk.”
9.12: And they said, “A lie! Reveal it to us now.” So he said, “Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I have anointed you meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl.” ’ ”
9.13: And they hurried, and each one took his garment and put it under him on the top of the steps. And they blew a ram’s horn, saying, “Yahu reigns!”
9.14: Thus Yahu son of Yahoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Yoram - now Yoram had been guarding Ramoth Gil’aḏ, he and all Yisra’ĕl, against Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram.
9.15: But Meleḵ Yahoram had returned to Yizre’ĕl to recover from the wounds with which the Arameans had smitten him when he fought with Ḥaza’ĕl meleḵ of Aram - Yahu now said, “If this is your desire, let no one leave or escape from the city to go and make it known in Yizre’ĕl!”
9.16: And Yahu rode in a chariot and went to Yizre’ĕl, for Yoram was laid up there. And Aḥazyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah had come down to see Yoram.
9.17: And a watchman stood on the tower in Yizre’ĕl, and he saw the company of Yahu as he came, and said, “I see a company of men.” And Yahoram said, “Get a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him say, ‘Is there peace?’ ”
9.18: And the horseman went to meet him, and said, “Thus said the meleḵ, ‘Is there peace?’ ” And Yahu said, “What have you to do with peace? Turn around and follow me.” And the watchman spoke, saying, “The messenger went to them, but is not coming back.”
9.19: Then he sent out a second horseman who came to them, and said, “Thus said the meleḵ, ‘Is there peace?’ ” And Yahu answered, “What have you to do with peace? Turn around and follow me.”
9.20: And the watchman spoke, saying, “He went up to them and is not coming back. And the driving is like the driving of Yahu son of Nimshi, for he drives madly!”
9.21: Then Yahoram said, “Hitch up.” And his chariot was hitched up. And Yahoram meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl and Aḥazyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah went out, each in his chariot. And they went out to meet Yahu, and met him on the portion of Naḇoth the Yizre’ĕlite.
9.22: And it came to be, when Yahoram saw Yahu, that he said, “Is there peace, Yahu?” But he answered, “What peace, as long as the whorings of your mother Izeḇel and her witchcraft are so many?”
9.23: Thereupon Yahoram turned his hands around and fled, and said to Aḥazyahu, “Treachery, O Aḥazyahu!”
9.24: And Yahu drew his bow and shot Yahoram between his arms. And the arrow came out at his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.
9.25: And said to Biḏqar his officer, “Take him up, and throw him into the portion of the field of Naḇoth the Yizre’ĕlite. Remember how you and I were riding together behind Aḥaḇ his father, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 lifted up this pronouncement against him:
9.26: ‘Have I not seen the blood of Naḇoth and the blood of his sons last night?’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. ‘And I shall repay you in this portion,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And now, take up, throw him on the portion, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
9.27: And Aḥazyahu meleḵ of Yahuḏah saw this and fled up the way to Bĕyth ha’Gan. And Yahu pursued him, and said, “Smite him, him too, in the chariot,” at the ascent to Gur, which is by Yiḇle’am. And he fled to Meḡiddo, and died there.
9.28: Then his servants conveyed him in the chariot to Yerushalayim, and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the City of Dawiḏ.
9.29: And in the eleventh year of Yoram son of Aḥaḇ, Aḥazyahu began to reign over Yahuḏah.
9.30: And Yahu came to Yizre’ĕl, and Izeḇel heard of it. And she put paint on her eyes and adorned her head, and looked through a window.
9.31: And as Yahu came to the gate, she said, “Is it peace, Zimri, slayer of your master?”
9.32: And he lifted up his face to the window and said, “Who is with me? Who?” And two, three eunuchs looked down to him.
9.33: And he said, “Throw her down.” And they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her under foot.
9.34: And he went in, and he ate and drank, and said, “Go now, see to this cursed one, and bury her, for she was a meleḵ’s daughter.”
9.35: So they went to bury her, but all they found of her was the skull and the feet and the palms of the hands.
9.36: And they came back and informed him. And he said, “This is the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, which He spoke by His servant Ĕliyahu the Tishbite, saying, ‘In the portion of Yizre’ĕl dogs are going to eat the flesh of Izeḇel,
9.37: and the corpse of Izeḇel shall be as dung on the surface of the field, in the portion of Yizre’ĕl, so that they do not say, “This is Izeḇel.” ’ ”
